sections.title: Recognition
sections.text: Imleria badia has a smooth, convex chestnut to bay-brown cap. It may be slightly sticky in wet weather and become drier with age. The underside consists of tubes ending in small cream to greenish-yellow pores that bruise blue. The light brown to ochre stem has no reticulation, but is often finely fibrillose or marbled rather than perfectly smooth.

sections.title: Cut surface and useful characters
sections.text: The flesh is whitish to yellowish and firm. It may stain slightly blue, especially near the tubes and in the upper stem. The pores are fine and round. The spore print is olive-brown. Bluing and the absence of a net are clues among several, not enough for identification on their own.

sections.title: Habitat and season
sections.text: This ectomycorrhizal bolete is common under conifers, especially pines, often on acidic or non-calcareous soils, though it can also occur near broad-leaved trees. It fruits mainly from summer into autumn, depending on climate and habitat.

sections.title: Lookalikes and safety
sections.text: A reticulated stem, red pores or a different overall form should prompt a fresh identification; no single character is conclusive. Raw or undercooked specimens can cause digestive symptoms. Tox Info Suisse recommends at least 20 minutes of cooking for this species. Never eat a wild mushroom based on a page or image; have the collection checked by an expert.

traits: Chestnut to bay-brown cap, fairly uniform, 5 to 15 cm, slightly sticky when young then dry; margin rolled in young ones
Tubes whitish then greenish yellow; fine pores of the same colour that turn clearly blue when pressed or cut
Cylindrical light-brown to ochre stem, without a net but often finely fibrillose or marbled
Whitish, firm flesh that turns a little blue above the tubes · faint smell, mild taste
Mostly under conifers, on moss or humus, non-chalky soil · summer to autumn
safetyNote: Eat only well cooked: Tox Info Suisse asks for at least 20 minutes of cooking. The bluing is not a sign of poison. No net on the stem, no red pores: otherwise it is not a bay bolete.
